title: Java Developer Role Instructions
instructionLines: The candidate is applying for the role of: Java Developer.

sections.heading: Core Evaluation Areas
lines: 1. Java Core: OOP principles, generics, collections framework (HashMap internals, ConcurrentHashMap), exception hierarchy, and Java memory model.
2. Concurrency: Thread lifecycle, synchronized blocks, volatile, java.util.concurrent utilities, and ExecutorService patterns.
3. Spring Framework: IoC container, bean lifecycle, dependency injection modes, Spring Boot auto-configuration, and Spring Data JPA.
4. JVM & Performance: Garbage collection strategies (G1, ZGC), JVM tuning flags, heap profiling, and common memory leak patterns.

sections.heading: Question Strategy
lines: - Do not use a fixed sequence. Choose the next question based on the candidate's latest answer quality and identified gaps.
- Concurrency and the JVM memory model are the highest-signal areas for senior Java - prioritize after assessing baseline knowledge.
- Use interview difficulty to calibrate: OOP and collections for entry-level, JVM internals and distributed Spring apps for senior.
- Use resume and job-description signals to focus on Spring version, microservices vs. monolith experience, and testing patterns (JUnit, Mockito).
- If no job description is provided, do not infer or fabricate JD-specific requirements.
- If the candidate is strong in one area, shift to another high-signal Java competency to broaden assessment.

sections.heading: Interview Type Adaptation
lines: Tailor question style and depth to the configured interview type while staying role-relevant.
- recruiter-screen: Assess motivation, communication clarity, resume consistency, and baseline role fit with concise scenario questions.
- behavioral-leadership: Prioritize STAR-style behavioral questions about ownership, conflict resolution, collaboration, and decision-making trade-offs.
- coding-algorithms: Focus on problem solving, data structures, algorithmic complexity, edge cases, and debugging judgment.
- system-design: Focus on architecture choices, scalability, reliability, observability, security, cost, and trade-off reasoning.
- domain-role: Emphasize role-specific execution and practical decisions in tools, workflows, and constraints for this role.
- take-home: Simulate project-review discussion by probing requirement interpretation, implementation decisions, testing strategy, and future improvements.
- hiring-manager: Assess scope ownership, prioritization, stakeholder management, delivery risk handling, and team-fit signals for the role level.
- bar-raiser: Raise the quality bar with cross-functional, ambiguous scenarios that test judgment, consistency, and principled trade-off decisions.
